Act as the implementation sub-agent for this task.

Implement GitHub issue #200 in indkhan/Moneo: "Steer a running Claude answer with follow-up messages". Read the issue first (`gh issue view 200`). Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly (tests policy, QA backend only, commit style, never touch the owner's backend/.env or port 3000).

Context: you are in a worktree created from branch `t3/claude-subscription` (PR #201, not yet merged). That PR adds a Claude-plan AI source: `lib/ai/claude.ts` (`claudeModel` wraps `ai-sdk-provider-claude-code` v4, which runs the Claude Agent SDK's bundled Claude Code with the owner's claude.ai login; Claude Code runs the whole tool loop inside one AI SDK step), `lib/ai/provider.ts` (`withTools`). In `app/api/chat/route.ts`, `prepareStep` takes steer messages via the `take_chat_steers` RPC and appends them before the next model step, then emits `{type:"steered"}`. On Claude that only happens once before the run, so mid-answer steers wait for the next turn.

Goal: on Claude, a steer sent during a running answer should reach that answer. Investigate the adapter (node_modules/ai-sdk-provider-claude-code/dist/index.d.ts and index.js: look for `streamingInput`, `onQueryCreated`, `onQueryControllerCreated`, `createClaudeCodeQueryController`, and how it feeds user messages) and the Agent SDK's streaming-input support. Prefer the smallest design: e.g. while a Claude run is active, poll/claim steers (reuse the existing take_chat_steers claim so a steer is never taken twice or lost) and push them into the running query as user messages, emitting the same `steered` event. Steers must still be claimed exactly once; if the run ends before a steer is delivered it must stay pending for the next turn as today. Keep ChatGPT/API-key behaviour unchanged. Make sure cancellation still stops everything and no timers/processes leak.

Tests: a focused unit test with a fake query controller/adapter that fails if a steer claimed during a run is not delivered, or is delivered twice. Use fake timers or controlled promises, no real waits (lint rule enforces this). No UI-copy tests.

Verify: `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`. No real Claude calls in tests. If you do one optional manual check against the QA backend, use a free port (3100 may be taken by another checkout; see scripts/qa-server.mjs) and only the moneo-qa stack.

If streaming input turns out not to be feasible with this adapter version, stop, document precisely why in the issue as a comment, and report back instead of building a workaround.

Deliver: commit in small plain-language commits (end each message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`), push a new branch `t3/claude-steering`, and open a PR with base `t3/claude-subscription` (stacked on PR #201) that says "Closes #200" and ends with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)". Never merge. Your final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

On ChatGPT and API keys, messages sent while an answer is running join it before the next model step (prepareStep in app/api/chat/route.ts takes them with take_chat_steers). With a Claude plan (#192), Claude Code runs the whole tool loop inside one AI SDK step, so prepareStep only runs before it starts: messages sent mid-answer wait for the next turn instead of steering this one.

The Agent SDK supports streaming input, so steers could be pushed into the running query. Done when a steer sent during a Claude answer changes that answer, as it does on ChatGPT.

content.text:
Steers sent during a Claude answer now reach that answer. The PR is open and stacked on #201. I didn't run it against a real Claude or the QA backend, so that path has only been tested with a fake adapter.

The adapter supports streaming input (`streamingInput: "always"`, `onStreamStart`). While a Claude answer runs, steers are claimed every 1.5 seconds with the existing `take_chat_steers` call, one claim at a time. Each is pushed into the running query as a user message.

- **Delivery:** the `steered` event is sent only once a steer actually reached the answer. If the answer ends while a claim is in flight, that steer is not injected and stays in the owner's queue to go out as the next message. The claim has already written its transcript row, so in that rare case the message shows twice in the conversation.
- **Cleanup:** polling stops and the timer clears when the answer finishes, fails or is canceled.
- **Other sources:** ChatGPT and API-key answers are unchanged. Claude calls without steering get no streaming input.
- **Tests:** a fake adapter with fake timers checks that a steer is delivered once, and that polling stops and a late claim is dropped on finish, failure and cancel. `npm test`, lint, typecheck and build pass. Five existing UI and page tests timed out at 5 seconds on this loaded machine, and the four I re-ran alone passed with a longer timeout. I did not re-run `migration-replay.test.ts`, which also failed in the full run.

Only the GitGuardian check had reported when I looked. Nothing has reviewed the PR yet.
